subject.title: fix(exec): stop isolated state dirs from moving live approvals

question: Should intentional bare OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR relocation retain the shipped direct-doctor approval migration, or should every custom state directory become independent even when an upgrade leaves existing restrictive approval policy behind?
rationale: Source and documentation establish the direct migration as an upgrade contract, while the incident demonstrates that state-root intent cannot be inferred safely; choosing between compatibility and absolute isolation defines a product security boundary.

options.title: Preserve explicit relocation
options.body: Keep automated and named-profile isolation, but retain a user-confirmed doctor migration for operators intentionally moving their primary state root.

options.title: Make all roots independent
options.body: Accept the breaking change, remove the migration, and provide maintainer-approved release guidance and an explicit manual policy-transfer workflow.

options.title: Pause for state identity
options.body: Hold the PR until OpenClaw can distinguish primary-root relocation from a genuinely independent instance without relying only on OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.

recommendation.title: Preserve explicit relocation
recommendation.body: Keep automated and named-profile isolation, but retain a user-confirmed doctor migration for operators intentionally moving their primary state root.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged guard and this broader follow-up make this person the strongest history-backed owner of the boundary decision.
